lesson_title: The Real Price of a T-shirt
hook_text: A T-shirt costs less than a meal. So who paid the rest of the price?
clip_script: Paarl, one cheap T-shirt. Its label says made in a faraway factory. Behind it are cotton farmers paid very little, factory workers sewing for long hours for low wages, sometimes in unsafe buildings. In 2013, a factory building in Bangladesh collapsed and more than a thousand garment workers died. Unfair trade means some people work hard but get an unfair share. Exploitation means using people unfairly for profit. Fair trade asks everyone in the chain to be treated fairly.
visual_style: Whiteboard T-shirt with a price tag, the tag unfolding into a chain of farmers, factory workers and shops, with the biggest share of money flowing to the end.
mood: Serious and caring, like a conversation that matters.
pacing: Calm opening with the T-shirt, slow walk down the chain, ending on what fairness means.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and talk with your family about what fair pay means.
